topic: cross-thread topic identity and incremental continuity in work communication
executive_summary: The literature strongly supports treating longitudinal work-matter identity as an open-world, incremental identity-resolution problem rather than ordinary semantic clustering. Continuation decisions should combine multiple identity-bearing signals, permit abstention, and preserve sufficient historical evidence for later merge or split correction. Incremental entity-resolution work shows that localized reassessment can approach batch quality while avoiding full recomputation, but naive incremental assignment can become order-dependent. Event-coreference research shows that action similarity alone is insufficient across domains: participants, time, location, arguments, and context materially affect identity, while partial or quasi-identity can be non-transitive. New-event and selective-classification work further supports an explicit UNCERTAIN/reject outcome rather than forcing attachment or novelty. However, the evidence is primarily from news, Wikipedia, entity resolution, image recognition, and public-record linkage; none establishes production accuracy for cross-thread email and Teams work matters.
themes: Identity requires evidence beyond semantic similarity: action, participants, time, location, arguments, references, and context contribute differently across datasets [2011.12249] [doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-58] [doi-10-1002-sim-4780140510].
Open-world rejection and abstention are first-class mechanisms for avoiding forced assignment when evidence is insufficient [1412.5687] [1705.08500] [doi-10-1145-354756-354843].
Incremental identity resolution can update only affected historical state and still approach batch-resolution quality [1402.4417] [doi-10-1007-978-3-030-49461-2-23].
Correction requires retained historical linkage structure; aggressive state compression can reduce future repairability [doi-10-1007-978-3-030-49461-2-23].
Benchmark-specific structure can improve in-domain results yet cause poor cross-corpus generalization [2011.12249] [2104.05022] [manual-e988e24127].
Partial or quasi-identity may be non-transitive, so not every related event should be collapsed into one identity cluster [manual-c43ffe3135].
Retrieval can narrow large historical collections before an expensive identity judgment, but local retrieved context may still be insufficient [doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-58].

Evaluation should distinguish continuation/linking, novelty/new-event detection, clustering, and abstention rather than reporting one aggregate clustering score [manual-5c20fb0229] [1705.08500] [doi-10-1145-354756-354843].

findings.statement: Cross-document identity should be decided from multiple compatibility signals rather than semantic or action similarity alone; participant, temporal, spatial, argument, and contextual evidence materially affects identity decisions.
A system should support an explicit reject or UNCERTAIN outcome instead of forcing every incoming item to an existing identity or declaring it definitively new.

Incremental identity resolution can avoid reprocessing all historical data while retaining resolution quality close to batch processing, and new evidence can legitimately revise earlier identity structure.
Naive online attachment can be sensitive to arrival order; bounded local reclustering is a practical mechanism for repairing historical decisions and reducing that dependency.

Preserving historical relationship structure is important for later correction: compact representations that discard intra-cluster links can make subsequent merge or split repair harder or impossible for repair algorithms that depend on those links.

Conversation, topic, or document preclustering can improve coreference performance, but such structural partitions must not be treated as identity because benchmark-specific clustering assumptions can overfit and transfer poorly.

Relatedness and identity are not equivalent: partial event identity includes membership, subevent, and spatiotemporal-continuity relations that can violate transitivity, so forcing all related evidence into one cluster can over-merge.

A retrieval-first architecture is plausible for Phase 2 investigation: candidate historical evidence can be retrieved from a very large collection before detailed coreference assessment, but unresolved cases may require evidence beyond the local query-candidate pair.

Identity models and evaluation results transfer poorly across corpora with different mention distributions and structural assumptions, so strong performance on ECB+, WEC, or another single benchmark is insufficient evidence for workplace communication.

Evaluation for msgloom should separately measure continuation/link detection, new-Topic detection, clustering quality, abstention coverage, and false-merge versus false-split behavior rather than relying on one clustering metric.

contradictions.topic: Document/topic preclustering: useful signal versus unsafe identity shortcut
contradictions.note: On ECB+, document topic clustering materially improves event-coreference performance [manual-e988e24127], but cross-corpus analysis finds ECB+-specific preclustering and document-link assumptions can overfit and transfer poorly [2011.12249], with substantial WEC/ECB+ transfer degradation also reported [2104.05022]. For msgloom this is best interpreted as a boundary condition, not a true logical contradiction: Group or conversation structure can narrow candidates but should not define Topic identity.

contradictions.topic: Simple incremental attachment versus repair-oriented incremental clustering
contradictions.note: Incremental ERLD reports quality close to batch resolution while processing affected state [1402.4417], whereas the multi-source FAMER study shows simple incremental max-both assignment can be arrival-order sensitive and that local reclustering is needed to recover batch-like quality [doi-10-1007-978-3-030-49461-2-23]. The difference suggests that repair requirements depend on matching errors, graph structure, and arrival pattern.

contradictions.topic: Transitive cluster identity versus non-transitive relatedness
contradictions.note: Entity-resolution methods operate naturally with transitive identity clusters [1402.4417] [doi-10-1007-978-3-030-49461-2-23], while dense event annotation finds important partial-identity relations that may violate transitivity [manual-c43ffe3135]. Msgloom should therefore keep Topic identity itself coherent while representing subevent, continuation-like, or uncertain relations separately instead of forcing them into the identity cluster.

contradictions.topic: Similarity-based tracking versus structure-aware identity modeling
contradictions.note: TDT results show that repeated full-text similarity tracking yields poor first-story detection at useful operating points [doi-10-1145-354756-354843], while later event-coreference work finds material value in participants, time, arguments, and explicit coreference scoring [2011.12249] [doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-58]. This argues against using embedding similarity alone as msgloom's identity rule.

gaps.description: There is no direct benchmark in this corpus for cross-thread, cross-channel concrete work-matter identity in enterprise email and chat, including same customer/project but distinct matters, multi-matter messages, and long-lived matters that change titles or channels.
gaps.suggested_query: "work item identity" email chat cross-thread enterprise OR "cross-channel" conversation linking work matter

gaps.description: The corpus does not establish a calibrated decision rule for CONTINUE versus NEW versus UNCERTAIN under asymmetric costs where false merges are substantially more damaging than false splits.
gaps.suggested_query: "event coreference" abstention reject option open set OR "cluster assignment" abstention asymmetric cost

gaps.description: More evidence is needed on partial identity, event evolution, and multiple simultaneous work matters when one incoming message contains spans that continue different historical identities.
gaps.suggested_query: "partial event coreference" event evolution subevent cross-document multi-event

gaps.description: Design and benchmark a msgloom-specific multi-signal matcher using independent synthetic/adversarial fixtures and transfer datasets, explicitly measuring false merges, false splits, NEW detection, UNCERTAIN coverage, and insertion-order sensitivity.

Define the stable Topic-ID and correction data model: immutable source evidence, versioned identity assessments, CONTINUE/NEW/UNCERTAIN decisions, merge/split corrections, supersession or alias links, and reconstructable history.
Determine the minimum historical evidence graph that must be retained to support bounded reclustering and later merge/split correction without keeping unnecessary derived state.

Benchmark candidate-retrieval strategies for Phase 2, measuring historical-candidate recall, latency, and downstream identity accuracy before choosing dense retrieval, sparse retrieval, deterministic indexes, or a hybrid.
Optimization of generated Topic titles or labels is not an identity problem; titles are presentation metadata and should not be used as stable Topic identifiers.

actionable_insights: Represent Topic identity with stable internal IDs independent of generated titles, subjects, conversation IDs, or source-specific thread IDs.

In Phase 1, link a candidate to an existing Topic only when supplied evidence positively supports identity; otherwise preserve the candidate separately with an explicit UNCERTAIN relationship rather than forcing CONTINUE or NEW.
Use semantic similarity, subject, participants, customer/project names, and conversation ancestry primarily for candidate generation; require additional identity-compatible evidence before merging.

Combine positive and negative evidence across action/object, participants, time, location, referenced artifacts, commitments, state compatibility, and source relationships; argument or temporal conflicts should be able to veto a superficially similar match.
Persist versioned identity assessments and provenance so later MERGE or SPLIT corrections add history instead of rewriting earlier source evidence or silently changing Topic meaning.

Retain enough pairwise or graph-level historical linkage evidence to support bounded local reclustering; do not irreversibly fuse clusters into representations that destroy the evidence needed for repair.
Test incremental assignment under adversarial insertion orders and delayed evidence, because arrival order can change results when repair is weak.
Calibrate a reject/UNCERTAIN threshold using risk-coverage style evaluation and explicitly assign a higher cost to false merges than false splits for msgloom's reporting objective.
For Phase 2, retrieve a bounded set of historical candidate Topics and supporting evidence, then rerun the identity assessment rather than searching the entire history inside every Phase 1 decision.
Evaluate continuation, novelty, uncertainty, merge repair, and split repair separately; aggregate clustering F1 alone can hide the failure modes that matter most to missed or duplicated work.
confidence_summary: Confidence is HIGH for the architectural conclusions that identity should be multi-signal, incremental, repairable, and allowed to abstain: these mechanisms recur across entity resolution, event coreference, open-world recognition, selective classification, and TDT. Confidence is also HIGH that single-benchmark results do not transfer reliably. Confidence is MEDIUM for the exact decision policy msgloom should use because no paper directly evaluates enterprise email/Teams work-matter identity, asymmetric false-merge costs, or msgloom's five-way CONTINUE/NEW/UNCERTAIN/MERGE/SPLIT contract. Transfer evidence justifies mechanisms and engineering experiments, not production-domain accuracy claims.
limitations: No paper in the corpus directly evaluates concrete work-matter identity across enterprise email and Teams or an equivalent work-communication domain.

Several strong results come from news or Wikipedia event coreference, whose event distributions, annotation assumptions, and document structures differ materially from workplace communication [2011.12249] [2104.05022] [doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-58].
Open-world and selective-classification papers use image recognition, so they support abstention and calibration mechanisms but not text-identity accuracy [1412.5687] [1705.08500].

Entity-resolution papers concern people, companies, or knowledge-graph entities; their transitive identity assumptions transfer imperfectly to evolving work matters [1402.4417] [doi-10-1007-978-3-030-49461-2-23].
The probabilistic public-health linkage paper and TDT overview were available only at abstract level, limiting inspection of experimental details [doi-10-1002-sim-4780140510] [manual-5c20fb0229].

Many event-coreference evaluations assume gold event mentions or pre-existing topic partitions, so they do not measure end-to-end errors from Topic-02 span detection or unrestricted historical candidate generation [2104.05022] [manual-c43ffe3135] [manual-e988e24127].

The synthesis cannot determine production thresholds, calibration values, or the acceptable UNCERTAIN coverage for msgloom without engineering evaluation on independently constructed fixtures and eventually authorized domain data.
